answer: Interviews is the technique considered the most commonly used by respondents for eliciting requirements in ML-enabled system projects. In the supplied data, 50.0% of the 194 valid respondents (97/194) quoted interviews as used, the highest share among all six Q9 elicitation techniques (Scenarios 38.66%, Prototyping 38.66%, Workshops/Meetings 38.14%, Observation 32.99%, Others 5.67%); a respondent-level bootstrap (B=10,000, seed=42) gives a 95% CI of [42.78%, 57.22%] for interviews. Note: the 69.399% [69.062, 69.735] quoted in the question is not exactly reproducible from this binarized CSV under any tested proportion definition (max observed is 50.0% at n=194, 35.1% at n=276; the stated CI half-width of ~0.34 pp is far narrower than a respondent-level bootstrap at n≈194), so the data-grounded value reported here is 50.0% on the 194 valid respondents, with interviews unambiguously the most common technique (ranking identical under the n=276 sensitivity).

payload.hypothesis: Interviews is the most commonly used technique for eliciting requirements in ML-enabled system projects: 50.0% of the 194 valid respondents (97/194) indicated using interviews, the highest share among the six Q9 techniques (Scenarios 38.66%, Prototyping 38.66%, Workshops/Meetings 38.14%, Observation 32.99%, Others 5.67%), with a respondent-level bootstrap 95% CI of [42.78%, 57.22%] (B=10,000, seed=42).
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded data/requirements_engineering_for_ML-enabled_systems.csv (276 respondents x 202 columns). 2) Mapped the no-answer block code '-77' to NaN on the six Q9_ML_Elicitation_* variables and restricted the analysis to the 194 respondents with complete Q9 (the 82 excluded rows are exactly the 'Suspended (22)' respondents who skipped the block; '-99'/'-66' appear only in free-text fields). 3) Computed per-technique usage as the proportion of 'quoted' (used) among the 194 valid respondents. 4) Selected the most common technique by argmax of the proportions: Interviews (97/194 = 50.000%). 5) Ran a nonparametric respondent-level bootstrap (resampling the 194 rows with replacement, B=10,000, numpy default_rng seed=42), recomputing the 'quoted' proportion per technique in each resample, and took the 2.5th/97.5th percentiles as the 95% CI: Interviews [42.784, 57.216]; Scenarios [31.959, 45.361]; Prototyping [31.959, 45.361]; Workshops/Meetings [31.443, 44.845]; Observation [26.289, 39.691]; Others [2.577, 9.278]. 6) Sensitivity: with denominator 276 (suspended counted as not used) Interviews remains rank 1 (35.145%); the ranking is identical to the n=194 case. 7) Reproducibility note: the question's stated 69.399% [69.062, 69.735] is not reproducible from this binarized CSV under any tested proportion definition (max 50.0% at n=194; 127/183=69.3989% matches the point estimate but no Q9 column has that count, and the stated +/-0.34 pp CI is far narrower than a respondent-level bootstrap at n~194), so the data-grounded figure reported is 50.0% on 194 valid respondents.
